spellings that have a shorter escape, redundant or backtracking-prone
constructs, and calls where a plain string function (`strpos`,
`str_replace`, `trim`, `explode`, a `===` comparison) does the same job
faster. Only a few findings carry a fix (the plain-function replacements).

NullCoalescingOperatorCanBeUsed.summary:
Ternaries and small `if` constructs that pick a value when it "exists"
(`isset`, `!== null`, `array_key_exists`, truthiness of the owning object) and a
fallback otherwise can be collapsed into a single `??` expression, which is
shorter and easier to read.
NullCoalescingOperatorCanBeUsed.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| SUGGEST_SIMPLIFYING_TERNARIES | bool | true | Enables Form A (ternaries). |
| SUGGEST_SIMPLIFYING_IFS | bool | true | Enables Form B (`if` statements). |

Both upstream fixtures set only one option explicitly, but the other one keeps
its default `true`, so both forms are active in both runs.

NullPointerException.summary:
A value that may be `null` (nullable object parameter, nullable local
variable, call declared to return `?T`/`void`) is dereferenced — property or
method access, array access, invocation, `clone`, or passed to a parameter
that rejects null — without a preceding null check. At runtime this is an
"call to a member function on null"-style error.

Disabled by default (experimental upstream).

NumberParseUsesCurrencyType.summary: Parse currency with parseCurrency. Enabled by default; require positive semantic or local-flow proof.

ObGetCleanCanBeUsed.summary:
Reading the output buffer with `ob_get_contents()` and then discarding it with
`ob_end_clean()` in the next statement is exactly what the single built-in
`ob_get_clean()` does. Merge the two calls.

OffsetOperations.summary:
Offset access `$x[...]` only works on arrays, strings and objects that
implement offset handling. Using it on a boolean, number or a plain object is
a bug (or a sign of missing type annotations); using an index whose type the
container does not accept (an array as a key, an object as a key) is also
flagged.

Disabled by default.

OneTimeUseVariables.summary:
A local variable that is assigned in one statement and consumed exactly once in
the very next `return`, `throw` or destructuring statement adds a name without
adding meaning. The value can be used directly at the consumption site.
OneTimeUseVariables.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ALLOW_LONG_STATEMENTS` | bool | false | When false, assignments whose text exceeds 80 characters are left alone (a long expression may deserve a name). When true, length is ignored. |
| `ANALYZE_RETURN_STATEMENTS` | bool | true | Inspect `return` consumers (D1). |
| `ANALYZE_THROW_STATEMENTS` | bool | true | Inspect `throw` consumers (D2). |
| `ANALYZE_ARRAY_DESTRUCTURING` | bool | true | Inspect `list()`/`[]` destructuring consumers (D3). |

OnlyWritesOnParameter.summary:
A parameter, closure import or local variable that is only ever written to
(elements appended, incremented, concatenated onto…) but never read is dead
work: the changes are lost when the function returns (by-value semantics).
Likewise a closure `use` import that the closure body never touches, or an
inline assignment whose target is never read afterwards, is unused.
OnlyWritesOnParameter.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `IGNORE_INCLUDES` | bool | `true` | When on, write-only findings are reported even if the scope contains `include`/`require` (which could read variables). When off, such scopes produce no W findings. U findings are unaffected. |

OpAssignShortSyntax.summary:
`$total = $total + $step` repeats the target; the compound assignment
`$total += $step` says the same thing more directly.

OpenSslEncryptionStatusUsedAsCiphertext.summary: Identify openssl_public_encrypt or openssl_private_encrypt status consumed by binary/text encoding or a string-output operation as ciphertext, while output parameter is a distinct variable.

OpenSslKeyLengthMismatch.summary: OpenSSL keys must match the chosen cipher's required byte length. Supply a correctly sized key instead of relying on padding or truncation.

OpenSslRawCiphertextOptionMismatch.summary: Raw ciphertext and base64-encoded ciphertext require different OpenSSL options. Use matching encoding options when decrypting an encryption result.

OpenSslSigningFailureIgnored.summary: Identify openssl_sign whose status is discarded and whose output signature is subsequently encoded, emitted or stored on an unconditional path.

OpenSslVerifyTruthyResult.summary: OpenSSL signature verification returns 1 for success, while an error result can also be truthy. Accept only the explicit success result.

OptionalRegexCaptureReadWithoutNullFlag.summary: An unmatched optional regex capture can be absent from the results. Guard the access or request null placeholders for unmatched captures.

OverrideAttributeWithoutTarget.summary: Apply Override to an inherited member.
OverrideAttributeWithoutTarget.options: None. Use ordinary rule configuration to enable or disable this inspection.

OwnedStreamNotClosed.summary: Detect an owned successfully opened stream leaving its local scope without close, return or ownership transfer.
OwnedStreamNotClosed.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

PackFormatArgumentMismatch.summary: Match pack values to the format.
PackFormatArgumentMismatch.options: None. Use normal rule configuration to enable or disable the inspection.

PackedHashtableOptimization.summary:
Since PHP 7 an array whose keys are integers inserted in ascending order can
be stored in a compact "packed" layout. An array literal that lists integer
keys out of order, or spells integer keys as numeric strings, misses that
layout. Sorting the keys or writing them as integers lets the engine use it.

ParameterDefaultValueIsNotNull.summary:
Optional parameters that may be "absent" are best expressed with a `null`
default (and a nullable type) rather than a sentinel such as `0`, `''` or
`[]`. This opt-in style rule flags non-null defaults where `null` could be used.

ParseStrKeyNormalizationMismatch.summary: parse_str normalizes dots and spaces in parameter names to underscores. Read the normalized key from the parsed result.

ParseUrlFailureDereferenced.summary: Identify ordinary unguarded reads of dynamic parse_url results, or literal results with a supported parsing-failure proof. Restrict to array-returning mode; missing keys are another concern.

ParsedQueryValueDecodedTwice.summary: parse_str already URL-decodes query values. Avoid a second decoding that changes encoded data into a different value.

PartialStreamWriteUnchecked.summary: Detect fwrite whose result is ignored or checked only against false when the complete payload is then claimed sent via unconditional return true.
PartialStreamWriteUnchecked.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

PassingByReferenceCorrectness.summary:
A parameter declared by reference (`&$p`) needs a variable-like argument.
Passing the result of a call that does not return by reference, or a `new`
expression, makes PHP emit a notice ("only variables should be passed by
reference") and the callee's writes are lost.

PasswordComparedWithFreshHash.summary: Detect password_hash result compared for equality with a stored string hash to decide password acceptance.
PasswordComparedWithFreshHash.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

PasswordUsedDirectlyAsEncryptionKey.summary: Encryption APIs do not derive a cryptographic key from a password. Apply an appropriate key derivation function before encrypting or decrypting. This inspection is disabled by default because the intended policy or use can vary.
PasswordUsedDirectlyAsEncryptionKey.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| passwordKeys | list | `["password", "passphrase"]` | Configure the explicit policy evidence described in D1. |

PasswordVerifyArgumentsReversed.summary: Identify password_verify when argument one is the unchanged output of password_hash(argument two), with both same-scope identities proven.

PathContainmentPrefixBoundary.summary: Detect canonical-path containment accepted through str_starts_with or equivalent prefix comparison against a literal non-root directory prefix without a directory-separator boundary.
PathContainmentPrefixBoundary.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

PdoApiUsage.summary:
Preparing a statement with `PDO::prepare()` and immediately running it with an
argument-less `execute()` gains nothing from the prepare step: no parameters
are bound. A single `PDO::query()` call does the same job.

PdoArrayBoundToSinglePlaceholder.summary: A single PDO placeholder cannot expand an array into multiple SQL values. Create a separate placeholder for each list element.

PdoBoundValueAssumedLive.summary: Identify execute without parameters when a locally bound scalar variable was reassigned after bindValue and no rebind occurred. Only track resolved PDOStatement and same variable used as binding input; changing it may be intentional so disabled by default.

PdoExecZeroRejectedAsFailure.summary: Identify proven PDO::exec result negated or loosely compared with false in a failure branch throwing or returning false. Strict false excludes.

PdoExecuteArrayReplacesBindings.summary: Detect execute with a literal empty parameter array on a statement with previously established required bindValue/bindParam bindings.
PdoExecuteArrayReplacesBindings.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

PdoFetchBothLeaksDuplicateColumns.summary: PDO's combined fetch mode exposes numeric and named copies of each field. Select the intended row representation before JSON serialization. This inspection is disabled by default because the intended policy or use can vary.

PdoFetchColumnFalsyValueLoss.summary: Detect fetchColumn result used as a truthiness condition that skips successful zero or empty-string results.
PdoFetchColumnFalsyValueLoss.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

PdoFetchIntoRetainsSharedRows.summary: Identify array append of an unchanged fetch return in a loop when statement FETCH_INTO mode targets same known object on every fetch. Cloned snapshots and immediate single-row consumption exclude.

PdoGroupedFetchReadsRemovedColumn.summary: Identify read of first selected named column from a row in unchanged FETCH_GROUP combined with FETCH_ASSOC results. Require complete projection and mode knowledge; wildcard, duplicate names or ambiguous SQL exclude.

PdoIdentifierPlaceholder.summary: Detect PDO prepare with a parameter marker in a table-name position following FROM, JOIN, UPDATE or INTO in parsed literal SQL.
PdoIdentifierPlaceholder.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

PdoMixedPlaceholderStyles.summary: Detect PDO prepare with literal SQL containing both named and positional parameter markers outside quoted literals/comments.
PdoMixedPlaceholderStyles.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

PdoPlaceholderBindingMismatch.summary: Detect execute on a resolved PDOStatement whose literal prepared SQL requires markers absent from the complete effective binding set, or whose binding set has extra markers.
PdoPlaceholderBindingMismatch.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

PdoQuotedPlaceholder.summary: Detect execution supplying a named binding occurring only as a quoted SQL string literal rather than an actual marker.
PdoQuotedPlaceholder.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

PdoReferenceBindingVariableReuse.summary: Detect two distinct PDO markers bound through bindParam to the same scalar local identity, with its value changed between bindings and before execute.
PdoReferenceBindingVariableReuse.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

PdoRepeatedNamedMarkerWithoutEmulation.summary: Identify prepare on a proven PDO mysql native-preparation connection with EMULATE_PREPARES false and SQL containing repeated same named marker outside literals/comments. Exclude drivers permitting repetition, unresolved driver, emulation true and SQL parser uncertainty.

PdoSelectRowCountAssumption.summary: Detect rowCount on a PDOStatement prepared from a SELECT and used as a total result count under an explicitly enabled portable-count contract.
PdoSelectRowCountAssumption.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

PermissionModeWrittenInDecimal.summary: A decimal permission literal can represent a different bitmask from the intended octal notation. Write Unix permission masks with an explicit octal prefix. This inspection is disabled by default because the intended policy or use can vary.

PgAsyncDispatchAssumedQuerySuccess.summary: Inspect the asynchronous PostgreSQL result status.
PgAsyncDispatchAssumedQuerySuccess.options: None. Use normal rule configuration to enable or disable the inspection.

PgAsyncResultsNotDrained.summary: Drain all pending PostgreSQL results before another asynchronous query.
PgAsyncResultsNotDrained.options: None. Use normal rule configuration to enable or disable the inspection.

PgEscapedLiteralQuotedAgain.summary: Use the already quoted PostgreSQL literal directly.
PgEscapedLiteralQuotedAgain.options: None. Use normal rule configuration to enable or disable the inspection.

PgFetchedZeroRejected.summary: Distinguish PostgreSQL fetch failure from a zero value.
PgFetchedZeroRejected.options: None. Use normal rule configuration to enable or disable the inspection.

PgIdentifierEscapedAsLiteral.summary: Escape PostgreSQL identifiers with the identifier API.
PgIdentifierEscapedAsLiteral.options: None. Use normal rule configuration to enable or disable the inspection.

PgReturnedRowsUsedAsAffectedRows.summary: Identify pg_num_rows on unchanged successful pg_query result whose constant SQL is INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE without RETURNING. Parse literals/comments rather than substring matching.

PhpUnitDeprecations.summary:
Flags PHPUnit assertion APIs deprecated in the configured PHPUnit version:
the optional trailing parameters of `assertEquals()` / `assertNotEquals()`
(deprecated in 8.0 in favour of dedicated assertions) and the
`assertFileNotExists()` / `assertDirectoryNotExists()` assertions (deprecated
in 9.1 in favour of their `...DoesNotExist()` counterparts).
PhpUnitDeprecations.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PHP_UNIT_VERSION` | enum (`PHPUNIT70` … `PHPUNIT95`, see ordering above) | `PHPUNIT80` | PHPUnit version targeted by the project. D1/D2 need ≥ `PHPUNIT80`; D3 needs ≥ `PHPUNIT91`. Unset → inferred from the indexed PHPUnit (see Divergences). |

PhpUnitTests.summary:
A grab-bag of PHPUnit hygiene checks. On test method docblocks it validates the
targets of `@covers`, `@depends` and `@dataProvider`, flags a redundant `@test`
and (optionally) unnamed datasets. On assertion and mock-builder calls it
points at generic assertions that have a dedicated, more expressive PHPUnit
counterpart (`assertTrue(!$x)` → `assertNotTrue($x)`,
`assertSame(1, count($l))` → `assertCount(1, $l)`, `->will($this->returnValue(…))`
→ `->willReturn(…)`, …) and rewrites them.

The rule has two independent halves:

- **Part A** — docblock tags on methods (D1–D12).
- **Part B** — method calls whose name starts with `assert`, or is `expects`
  or `will` (D13–D30).

Neither half checks that the class extends a PHPUnit test case: every method
of every class-like and every matching method call is examined.
PhpUnitTests.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PHP_UNIT_VERSION` | enum | `PHPUNIT80` | Target PHPUnit version, one of `PHPUNIT70`, `PHPUNIT71`, `PHPUNIT72`, `PHPUNIT73`, `PHPUNIT74`, `PHPUNIT75`, `PHPUNIT80`, `PHPUNIT81`, `PHPUNIT82`, `PHPUNIT83`, `PHPUNIT84`, `PHPUNIT85`, `PHPUNIT90`, `PHPUNIT91`, `PHPUNIT92`, `PHPUNIT93`, `PHPUNIT94`, `PHPUNIT95` (ordered; comparisons are by this order). Below 8.0 D20 suggests `assertInternalType`/`assertNotInternalType`, from 8.0 `assertIs*`/`assertIsNot*`. D25 only runs below 9.0. D23 uses the `NotExists` negative names below 9.1 and `DoesNotExist` from 9.1. D26/D27 use `assertRegExp`/`assertNotRegExp` below 9.1 and `assertMatchesRegularExpression`/`assertDoesNotMatchRegularExpression` from 9.1. No other effect on detection or fixes. Conformance passes it as `PhpUnitVersion.PHPUNIT75` style values; strip the prefix. Unset → inferred from the indexed PHPUnit (see Divergences), else `PHPUNIT80`. |
| `SUGGEST_TO_USE_ASSERTSAME` | bool | `false` | Enables D17. |
| `SUGGEST_TO_USE_NAMED_DATASETS` | bool | `false` | Enables D6. |
| `PROMOTE_PHPUNIT_API` | bool | `true` | Enables D18–D28. |
| `PROMOTE_MOCKING_ONCE` | bool | `true` | Enables D29. |
| `PROMOTE_MOCKING_WILL_RETURN` | bool | `true` | Enables D30. |

PosixAccountLookupFailureDereferenced.summary: Identify array indexing on direct or unchanged posix_getpwnam/posix_getpwuid result without a dominating strict false rejection.

PotentialMalware.summary:
Flags code shapes typical of injected web-shells and backdoors: `eval()` of
decoded or fetched payloads, small decoder functions, timestamp forging
with `touch()`, and enumeration of all defined functions.

PowerOperatorCanBeUsed.summary:
Since PHP 5.6 exponentiation has its own operator. `pow($a, $b)` can be
written `$a ** $b`, which is shorter and avoids a function call.

PregMatchAllLayoutMismatch.summary: Regex result indices depend on whether output is grouped by capture or by match. Read indices consistent with the selected layout.

PregMatchFailureAsNonMatch.summary: Detect preg_match or preg_match_all tested with boolean negation or a falsy branch that handles input rejection without distinguishing false from zero.
PregMatchFailureAsNonMatch.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

PregQuoteUsage.summary:
`preg_quote()` only escapes the pattern delimiter when it is given as the
second argument. Called with a single argument, a `/` or `#` inside the quoted
text breaks the surrounding pattern.

PregQuoteUsedOnReplacement.summary: Pattern escaping can insert unwanted characters into replacement text. Keep literal replacements separate from regex pattern escaping.

PregReplaceFailureUnchecked.summary: Detect a nullable result of preg_replace or preg_replace_callback flowing into a non-null string parameter or dereference without a successful null guard.
PregReplaceFailureUnchecked.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

PregSplitCaptureFlagWithoutGroups.summary: Detect preg_split with PREG_SPLIT_DELIM_CAPTURE on a parsed literal regex containing no capturing groups.
PregSplitCaptureFlagWithoutGroups.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

PreloadingUsageCorrectness.summary:
In an opcache preload script, including files with `require`/`include`
executes them, which can fail on unresolved dependencies (PHP bug #78918).
`opcache_compile_file()` only compiles and caches the file, which is what a
preload script usually wants.

PrintfScanfArguments.summary:
The `printf`/`scanf` family takes as many value arguments as the format string
has conversions. A missing or extra argument silently produces wrong output
(or an `ArgumentCountError` in PHP 8), and a stray `%` makes the format
invalid.

PriorityQueueExtractionShapeMismatch.summary: Match the priority queue extraction mode.
PriorityQueueExtractionShapeMismatch.options: None. Use ordinary rule configuration to enable or disable this inspection.

PriorityQueueMinOrderAssumption.summary: Reverse priorities for smallest-first extraction. This opt-in inspection applies the policy stated in Detection.
PriorityQueueMinOrderAssumption.options: None. Enabling the rule declares the policy stated in Detection; the rule is disabled by default.

ProcessClosedBeforeOwnedPipes.summary: Waiting for a child process while its owned pipes remain open can deadlock. Close or drain the pipes before waiting for process exit.

ProcessExecFailureReportedAsSuccess.summary: Identify pcntl_exec followed immediately by exit(0) or exit without status in same straight-line scope; successful exec never returns.

ProcessExitCodeLostByRepeatedStatusRead.summary: Identify exitcode read from second proc_get_status after first same-process result proved running false in a dominating branch, on PHP before8.3 only.

ProcessPipeDirectionMisinterpreted.summary: Identify parent fwrite to proc_open pipe whose known descriptor mode is w, or parent fread/stream_get_contents on mode r. Child-relative r yields parent writable pipe; child-relative w yields parent readable pipe. Require successful process creation and exact pipe descriptor provenance.

ProcessPipesDrainedSequentially.summary: Reading a child's stdout and stderr sequentially can deadlock when the other pipe fills. Drain both output pipes concurrently. This inspection is disabled by default because the intended policy or use can vary.

ProperNullCoalescingOperatorUsage.summary:
Two misuses of `??`: (a) `call() ?? null` — a call result never triggers an
undefined-index/variable notice, so `?? null` does nothing; (b) a fallback
whose type has nothing in common with the left operand's type, which usually
signals a bug or a confusing API.
ProperNullCoalescingOperatorUsage.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| ANALYZE_TYPES | bool | true | Enables Case B (type complementarity). |
| ALLOW_OVERLAPPING_TYPES | bool | true | When true, any shared type makes operands complementary; when false, the right operand's types must cover all of the left operand's types. |

Upstream fixtures run with `ANALYZE_TYPES` = true and
`ALLOW_OVERLAPPING_TYPES` = false.

PropertyCanBeStatic.summary:
A non-public instance property initialised with a sizeable array literal
(several nested arrays or strings) is copied into every object. When such data
is really per-class configuration it is cheaper as a static property — or, on
PHP 5.6+, as a class constant.

PropertyInitializationFlaws.summary:
Property defaults and constructor assignments that do nothing: an explicit
`= null` default (untyped properties are already `null`), a default that
merely repeats the inherited one, a default on a private property that the
constructor unconditionally overwrites, and a constructor assignment that
writes exactly the default value.
PropertyInitializationFlaws.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REPORT_DEFAULTS_FLAWS` | bool | `true` | Enables Check 1 (N, S) and pattern O of Check 2. |
| `REPORT_INIT_FLAWS` | bool | `true` | Enables Check 2 (W, and O when the other option is on). |

RandomApiMigration.summary:
The libc-based `rand()` family is weaker and slower than the Mersenne Twister
family (`mt_*`), and since PHP 7.0 `random_int()` provides a CSPRNG integer.
Suggest renaming legacy random calls to their modern counterpart.
RandomApiMigration.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SUGGEST_USING_RANDOM_INT` | bool | `true` | When on and the level is 7.0+, `rand`/`mt_rand` with two arguments are pointed at `random_int`; when off, the classic table is used at every level. |

RangeZeroStep.summary: Identify range with a numeric step proven equal to zero; map supported named arguments.

ReadFromWriteOnlyStream.summary: Open the stream with read access.
ReadFromWriteOnlyStream.options: None. Use ordinary rule configuration to enable or disable this inspection.

ReadLoopProcessesEofFailure.summary: An EOF-tested loop can pass a failed read to a strict string consumer. Loop on the successful read result before processing a line.

ReadModifyWriteLockTooLate.summary: Detect file_get_contents of a path feeding a transformed value into file_put_contents on the same proven path with LOCK_EX but no enclosing lock spanning the read.
ReadModifyWriteLockTooLate.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

ReaddirFalsyFilenameLoss.summary: Compare the directory entry with false.
ReaddirFalsyFilenameLoss.options: None. Use ordinary rule configuration to enable or disable this inspection.

ReadonlyPropertyReassignment.summary: Detect assignment to a resolved readonly instance property already initialized on every reachable incoming path.
ReadonlyPropertyReassignment.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

RealpathFailureUsedAsPath.summary: Identify concatenation of an unchecked realpath result followed by consumption by a resolved filesystem path API; require local exact provenance.

RealpathInStreamContext.summary:
`realpath()` returns `false` for paths inside stream wrappers such as
`phar://`, so code that works on disk breaks once packaged. Climbing
directories with `realpath(__DIR__ . '/../')` or wrapping include paths in
`realpath()` should use `dirname()` / the plain path instead.

RecursiveReplaceRetainsListTail.summary: Recursive array replacement can leave entries from the end of an older list. Replace the list explicitly when the shorter list should remove that tail. This inspection is disabled by default because the intended policy or use can vary.

RecursiveTraversalOmitsDirectories.summary: Include parent nodes when traversing directories. This opt-in inspection applies the policy stated in Detection.
RecursiveTraversalOmitsDirectories.options: None. Enabling the rule declares the policy stated in Detection; the rule is disabled by default.

RedirectContinuesProtectedExecution.summary: Detect a conditional unauthorized branch emitting a Location header and falling through to an operation marked protected by the same authorization predicate.
RedirectContinuesProtectedExecution.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

RedundantElseClause.summary:
When an `if` body always leaves the current flow (return, throw, break,
continue, exit/die), the following `else`/`elseif` keyword is superfluous: its
code can simply follow the `if`. Removing it flattens nesting.

ReferencingObjects.summary:
Since PHP 5, object handles are passed and assigned by value of the handle:
the callee already works on the same object. Taking objects by reference
(`Foo &$x` parameters, `$x = &new Foo()`) is a PHP 4 leftover that only
confuses readers — unless the reference is really used to replace the
caller's variable.

ReflectionCompositeTypeAssumedNamed.summary: Inspect the composite reflection type members.
ReflectionCompositeTypeAssumedNamed.options: None. Use ordinary rule configuration to enable or disable this inspection.

ReflectionNamedArgumentMismatch.summary: Use a declared reflection parameter name.
ReflectionNamedArgumentMismatch.options: None. Use ordinary rule configuration to enable or disable this inspection.

RegexBodyDoesNotCompile.summary: Identify a constant slash or tilde delimited regex body with an unterminated ordinary character class or group, or unmatched closing parenthesis. Validate delimiter/modifier shape first. Exclude advanced (? syntax, extended mode, quoted \Q regions, escapes not fully parsed and paired delimiters; no Go regexp parser may reject valid PCRE features.

RegexByteOffsetAsCharacterOffset.summary: Detect a PREG_OFFSET_CAPTURE byte offset flowing into the start argument of mb_substr or grapheme_substr for the same proven string value.
RegexByteOffsetAsCharacterOffset.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

RegexReplacementCallbackFallsThrough.summary: Identify preg_replace_callback with an inline callback having a reachable fallthrough path and no generator semantics. An explicit return on every path excludes.

RegexReplacementReferencesMissingGroup.summary: Identify preg_replace with constant pattern and constant replacement referencing a numeric group absent from a fully parsed pattern. Support dollar and backslash forms and escaping; exclude branch-reset or conditional syntax if exact group numbering cannot be proved.

RegexUtf8SubjectKnownInvalid.summary: Identify preg_match, preg_match_all, preg_replace or preg_split with known u modifier and a constant subject whose bytes fail strict UTF-8 validation; exclude byte-oriented patterns.

RelativeSymlinkTargetUsesWrongBase.summary: Identify direct readlink result passed as a filesystem path when same scope proves the symlink target is relative and the link path directory differs from known current directory. A relative link target alone cannot prove the cwd mismatch; unknown cwd excludes.

RenameFailureUnchecked.summary: Renaming a file can fail. Check the result before returning success from the publication operation. This inspection is disabled by default because the intended policy or use can vary.

RepeatedCookieHeaderReplacement.summary: Detect a second header call with a Set-Cookie literal and default/true replace flag on a path with an earlier Set-Cookie header.
RepeatedCookieHeaderReplacement.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

RepeatedHtmlEntityEncoding.summary: Detect htmlspecialchars or htmlentities directly nesting an equivalent encoding call with matching flags/encoding and default or true double_encode.
RepeatedHtmlEntityEncoding.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

RequestControlledSessionId.summary: Accepting a session identifier from request data can let a caller choose the session being used. Generate identifiers independently of untrusted input.

ReturnTypeCanBeDeclared.summary:
A method without a declared return type whose returned values (and `@return`
documentation) all agree on one type — optionally nullable, or nothing at all
(`void`) — can carry a native return type declaration. Declaring it lets the
engine enforce the contract and documents it in the signature.
ReturnTypeCanBeDeclared.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| LOOKUP_PHPDOC_RETURN_DECLARATIONS | bool | true | Lets `@return self` / `@return $this` turn a class-typed suggestion into `self` (compact step 1). |

SameSiteNoneWithoutSecure.summary: Detect setcookie with literal options selecting SameSite None and secure absent or false.
SameSiteNoneWithoutSecure.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

ScandirFailureIterated.summary: Identify foreach iterable directly produced by scandir or its unchanged local result without a dominating false-rejecting guard.

SecretstreamPushAfterFinalTag.summary: Identify secretstream push on same local state after a prior push using TAG_FINAL, with unchanged state identity.

SecurityAdvisories.summary:
Works on a project's `composer.json` (not on PHP code). Two concerns:
development-only packages (test frameworks, debuggers, static analysers…)
listed under `require` end up in production; and an application that pulls
third-party packages should also require the advisory "firewall" meta-package
in `require-dev`, which blocks installing versions with known
vulnerabilities.

Throughout this spec:

- **ADV** is the advisory meta-package: vendor `roave`, package
  `security-advisories`; its full name is vendor, `/`, package.
- **CHK** is the alternative checker package: vendor `sensiolabs`, package
  `security-checker`.
- **DEV** is the effective development-package list (option
  `optionConfiguration`, see Options).
SecurityAdvisories.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REPORT_MISSING_ROAVE_ADVISORIES` | bool | false | Enables kinds A (missing advisory package, with fix) and L (advisory package not on `dev-latest`). |
| `REPORT_MISPLACED_DEPENDENCIES` | bool | true | Enables kind M (development packages under `require`). |
| `optionConfiguration` | list of strings | the default list below | The development-package list DEV, used for kind M and for the owner skip (D2). |

Effective DEV: upstream always merges the default list into whatever the
user configured (user entries ∪ defaults, deduplicated). Recommendation for
custos: DEV = defaults ∪ user entries. Entries may also be vendor prefixes
ending in `/` (only meaningful for the owner skip D2).

Conformance note: upstream test cases that do not add the defaults run with
an *empty* DEV (the merge happens only when settings are loaded). With the
upstream fixtures this makes no difference to the outcome, except that the
two cases which explicitly add the defaults are the only ones where kind M
or the owner skip can fire. Using the defaults always is safe.

SeekSuccessCheckedAsTruthy.summary: Compare the seek result with zero.
SeekSuccessCheckedAsTruthy.options: None. Use ordinary rule configuration to enable or disable this inspection.

SelectFailureTreatedAsReadiness.summary: Handle selection failure before processing ready streams.

SelectWatchArraysNotRestored.summary: Restore stream watch arrays before each selection. This opt-in rule applies the policy described in Detection.

SelfClassReferencing.summary:
Inside a class's own methods, refer to the class consistently: by default with
`self` (and `__CLASS__` instead of `Name::class`), which survives renames; or,
when `PREFER_CLASS_NAMES` is on, with the explicit class name instead of `self`
/ `__CLASS__`.
SelfClassReferencing.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| PREFER_CLASS_NAMES | bool | false | Switches the preferred style: false = use `self`/`__CLASS__`; true = use the explicit class name / `Name::class`. |

SemaphoreFailureEntersCriticalSection.summary: Identify discarded sem_acquire with nonblocking true followed by resolved shm_put_var/shm_remove_var and then sem_release of the same unchanged semaphore in the same straight-line scope. The acquire/mutate/release structure establishes explicit locking behavior; arbitrary custom functions cannot prove this contract and are excluded.

SenselessMethodDuplication.summary:
A child class method whose body is a copy of the inherited method's body is
dead weight: if the visibility is the same the override can simply be
deleted; if only the visibility differs, the override should delegate to
`parent::` instead of duplicating the code.
SenselessMethodDuplication.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MAX_METHOD_SIZE` | int | `20` | Methods with more top-level statements than this are skipped. |

SenselessProxyMethod.summary:
An override whose only statement forwards its parameters unchanged to the
same-named parent method — with the same signature, modifiers and
documentation tags — adds nothing; inheritance already provides that
behaviour. Remove it.

SenselessTernaryOperator.summary:
`$a === $b ? $a : $b` always evaluates to `$b`: when the two are identical it
does not matter which one is returned. The same holds for `!==` with swapped
branches. Such ternaries only add branching; replace them with the operand
that is always the result.

SessionCookieOptionsSetAfterStart.summary: Detect session_set_cookie_params after a successfully active session_start with no intervening close/destroy.
SessionCookieOptionsSetAfterStart.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

SessionDestroyLeavesLocalAuthentication.summary: Destroying stored session data does not clear the current session array. Clear local authentication state before reading it again.

SessionLockHeldDuringBlockingCall.summary: Detect a known blocking sleep/usleep or network operation while an active session with a known locking handler remains owned by the scope.
SessionLockHeldDuringBlockingCall.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

SessionMutationAfterClose.summary: Detect a write to $_SESSION after successful session_write_close and before a proven session_start reopening.
SessionMutationAfterClose.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

SessionNameChangedWhileActive.summary: A session name must be configured before the session becomes active. Set the name before starting the session.

SessionRegenerationFailureUnchecked.summary: Session identifier regeneration can fail. Check its result before establishing the configured authenticated session state. This inspection is disabled by default because the intended policy or use can vary.
SessionRegenerationFailureUnchecked.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| authenticationKeys | list | `["authenticated"]` | Configure the explicit policy evidence described in D1. |

ShallowCloneNestedMutation.summary: Detect cloning an object followed by mutation of a nested object member where the nested identity is proven shared with the original.
ShallowCloneNestedMutation.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

SharedLockUsedForWriting.summary: A shared lock does not provide exclusive access for a write. Acquire an exclusive lock before changing the protected stream.

SharedMemoryWriteCapacityExceeded.summary: Identify shmop_write with constant data length greater than remaining capacity established by offset shmop_size(same segment) minus positive constant. Also support exact known segment size. Unknown byte lengths or capacity exclude.

ShortEchoTagCanBeUsed.summary:
In templates, a PHP block that only outputs something — `<?php echo $x ?>` —
reads better as the short echo tag `<?= $x ?>`.

ShortListSyntaxCanBeUsed.summary:
From PHP 7.1 destructuring can use the short `[...]` form instead of
`list(...)`, consistent with short array syntax.

ShortOpenTagUsage.summary:
The short open tag `<?` depends on the `short_open_tag` ini setting; code using
it breaks (prints source code) where that setting is off. Use `<?php`.

ShortStreamReadUnchecked.summary: Detect fread with a fixed positive byte count whose result reaches unpack requiring that exact length without a length check.
ShortStreamReadUnchecked.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

SignalHandlerHasNoDispatchMechanism.summary: Dispatch signals when asynchronous handling is disabled.

SignalRegistrationFailureReportedAsSucce.summary: Identify discarded pcntl_signal immediately followed by unconditional return true in same function.

SignalWaitFailureAcceptedAsSignal.summary: Identify truthiness test of pcntl_sigwaitinfo result followed by passing that unchanged result to a call in true branch. Failure -1 is truthy; explicit >0 or !== -1 excludes.

SimpleXmlChildValueContainsBareAmpersand.summary: Identify SimpleXMLElement::addChild value with known ampersand not part of a valid entity/reference. Exclude named entities whose declarations may come from the document DTD, unknown values and name-only calls.

SimpleXmlLoadFileUsage.summary:
`simplexml_load_file()` is affected by a long-standing PHP bug (#62577) where
loading fails depending on the libxml entity-loader state. Reading the file
yourself and passing its contents to `simplexml_load_string()` avoids it.

SimpleXmlMissingNodeCheckedAsNull.summary: Identify strict null comparison on property access of a locally constructed SimpleXMLElement when its exact well-formed literal XML has no such child in matching namespace. Existing child, unknown XML or namespaces exclude.

SimpleXmlTextCastAsBoolean.summary: Identify boolean cast of a locally constructed SimpleXMLElement whose literal sole text content is a boolean spelling true/false and whose element has no children or attributes. Literal false produces true under object conversion; disabled by default because parsing intent remains optional.

SlowArrayOperationsInLoop.summary:
Two loop anti-patterns:

- **Accumulating merges**: `$acc = array_merge($acc, $chunk)` inside a loop
  copies the whole accumulator on every iteration (quadratic cost). Collect
  the chunks and merge once after the loop.
- **Length in a `for` condition**: `$i < count($items)` re-evaluates the
  length on every iteration. Compute it once in the initialiser.

SoapLastRequestWithoutTracing.summary: Identify __getLastRequest on locally constructed SoapClient whose options prove trace false or omitted default, without mutation or unknown calls. Unknown option maps exclude.

SoapNonWsdlRequiredOptionsMissing.summary: Identify new SoapClient with first argument null and fully known options array missing uri or location. Unpacked or dynamically keyed options exclude.

SocketReadZeroRejected.summary: Identify socket_read in PHP_BINARY_READ mode tested by negation or loose false equality in a branch throwing or returning false. Strict false and explicit empty string checks exclude.

SodiumKdfContextLengthMismatch.summary: Identify sodium_crypto_kdf_derive_from_key whose context has known byte length other than SODIUM_CRYPTO_KDF_CONTEXTBYTES, eight.

SodiumNonceLengthMismatch.summary: Secretbox requires its defined nonce byte length. Construct the nonce using the extension's required-length constant.

SodiumSecretboxKeyLengthMismatch.summary: Identify sodium_crypto_secretbox or open when key byte length is proven other than SODIUM_CRYPTO_SECRETBOX_KEYBYTES; unknown length excludes.

SodiumSecretboxNonceReused.summary: Identify the second secretbox encryption on same proven key and nonce when plaintexts are proven distinct. Identical plaintexts, unknown equality, new nonce and new key exclude.

SortComparatorReturnsBoolean.summary: Detect usort, uasort, or uksort with a local comparator whose every returned value is boolean and at least one return is an ordering comparison.
SortComparatorReturnsBoolean.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

SortComparatorReturnsFloat.summary: Detect a builtin sort comparator returning a subtraction whose operands are proven floats.
SortComparatorReturnsFloat.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

SortResultUsedAsArray.summary: Detect the boolean result of sort, rsort, asort, arsort, ksort, krsort, usort, uasort, or uksort when consumed directly or through a proven alias by foreach or an array-only builtin.
SortResultUsedAsArray.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

SplFixedArrayIndexOutOfBounds.summary: Use an index within the fixed array size.
SplFixedArrayIndexOutOfBounds.options: None. Use ordinary rule configuration to enable or disable this inspection.

SplFixedArrayShrinkDiscardsValues.summary: Preserve populated entries before shrinking. This opt-in inspection applies the policy stated in Detection.
SplFixedArrayShrinkDiscardsValues.options: None. Enabling the rule declares the policy stated in Detection; the rule is disabled by default.

SplObjectStorageIndirectArrayMutation.summary: Assign the modified storage value back.
SplObjectStorageIndirectArrayMutation.options: None. Use ordinary rule configuration to enable or disable this inspection.

SqlNullComparedWithEquality.summary: SQL equality comparisons do not test whether a value is null. Use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL instead.

SqliteBindingIndexZero.summary: Start SQLite binding positions at one.
SqliteBindingIndexZero.options: None. Use normal rule configuration to enable or disable the inspection.

SqliteClearWithoutRequiredReset.summary: Reset the SQLite statement before rebinding cleared parameters.
SqliteClearWithoutRequiredReset.options: None. Use normal rule configuration to enable or disable the inspection.

SqliteFetchBothLeaksDuplicateColumns.summary: Fetch named SQLite columns before JSON serialization. This inspection is disabled by default; enabling it selects the stated policy.
SqliteFetchBothLeaksDuplicateColumns.options: None. Use normal rule configuration to enable or disable the inspection.

SqliteForeignKeySettingInsideTransaction.summary: Identify PRAGMA foreign_keys assignment inside a known active transaction on a resolved SQLite3 or PDO sqlite connection. Parse complete literal SQL statements; BEGIN opens, COMMIT/END/ROLLBACK close, and unknown transaction state excludes.

SqliteNondeterministicFunctionDeclaredDe.summary: Identify SQLite3::createFunction with SQLITE3_DETERMINISTIC when inline callback directly returns random_int, random_bytes, time or microtime, without composition. Unknown callback behavior cannot prove nondeterminism.

SqliteNullBindingDiscardsValue.summary: Pass null when using the SQLite null binding type.
SqliteNullBindingDiscardsValue.options: None. Use normal rule configuration to enable or disable the inspection.

SqliteResultUsedAfterFinalize.summary: Read the SQLite result before finalizing it.
SqliteResultUsedAfterFinalize.options: None. Use normal rule configuration to enable or disable the inspection.

StaticClosureCanBeUsed.summary:
A closure (or arrow function) that never touches the object it was created in
can be declared `static`. That prevents an implicit `$this` binding, makes the
scope explicit and avoids keeping the surrounding object alive.
StaticClosureCanBeUsed.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| SUGGEST_FOR_SHORT_FUNCTIONS | bool | true | When false, arrow functions are never reported. |

StaticInvocationViaThis.summary:
Calling a static method through an object (`$this->make()` or `$obj->make()`)
hides the fact that no instance is involved. Use `self::`/`ClassName::` so the
call reads as what it is.
StaticInvocationViaThis.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| EXCEPT_PHPUNIT_ASSERTIONS | bool | true | Skip static methods declared in PHPUnit framework classes and Symfony's test assertion traits (E3). |
| EXCEPT_ELOQUENT_MODELS | bool | true | Skip static methods declared in Laravel's Eloquent base model (E4). |

StaticLambdaBinding.summary:
A `static` closure or arrow function has no bound object: using `$this` in it,
or calling an instance method of the parent class through `parent::`, fails at
runtime. Either drop `static` or stop relying on the object.

StrContainsCanBeUsed.summary:
Comparing a `strpos()`/`mb_strpos()` result strictly against `false` is the
pre-PHP 8 idiom for "does the string contain this substring". PHP 8 has
`str_contains()` for exactly that.

StrEndsWithCanBeUsed.summary:
Cutting the tail off a string with `substr($h, -strlen($n))` and comparing it
to `$n` is the pre-PHP 8 "ends with" idiom. PHP 8 has `str_ends_with()`,
which is clearer and avoids building a temporary string.

StrStartsWithCanBeUsed.summary:
`strpos($h, $n) === 0` is the pre-PHP 8 way to ask "does `$h` begin with
`$n`". PHP 8 provides `str_starts_with()`, which says it directly and does not
scan the whole haystack.

StrStrUsedAsStrPos.summary:
`strstr()` / `stristr()` build and return a substring. When the result is only
used as a yes/no answer ("does the haystack contain the needle?"), that copy is
wasted work: a position search (`strpos()` / `stripos()`) compared strictly
against `false` answers the same question without allocating.
StrStrUsedAsStrPos.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | | | Operand order in the fix follows the global comparison style (`regular` default / `yoda`). |

StrTrUsageAsStrReplace.summary:
`strtr($subject, $from, $to)` with single-character `$from` and `$to` is really
a plain character replacement; `str_replace($from, $to, $subject)` states that intent
more clearly.

StreamOpenFailureUnchecked.summary: Detect fopen result passed to a stream-only operation without excluding false.
StreamOpenFailureUnchecked.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

StreamOutputReturnUsedAsContent.summary: Output the stream without printing its byte count.
StreamOutputReturnUsedAsContent.options: None. Use ordinary rule configuration to enable or disable this inspection.

StreamUseAfterClose.summary: Detect a stream operation requiring an open resource on an identity closed by a successful fclose on every incoming path.
StreamUseAfterClose.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

StringCaseManipulation.summary:
Lower- or upper-casing the haystack and/or needle only to make a substring
search case-insensitive costs extra string copies; PHP already ships
case-insensitive variants of the position functions (`stripos`, `strripos`,
`mb_stripos`, `mb_strripos`). Use them on the raw strings instead.

StringNormalization.summary:
Two smells when chaining string normalisation calls:

1. Changing the case of a string and *then* trimming / cutting it converts
   characters that are thrown away right after; cut first, convert the case
   of the (shorter) result.
2. Wrapping a case conversion inside another case conversion is pointless
   when the outer call overrides what the inner one did (or repeats it); the
   inner call can be dropped.

StringOffsetWriteTruncatesValue.summary: Identify assignment of a proven string longer than one byte to an integer offset on a value proven to be a string; multibyte character strings still count bytes.

StringPadEmptyPadding.summary: Identify str_pad with a proven empty pad string only when requested length exceeds known byte length of input.

StringRepeatNegativeCount.summary: Identify str_repeat when times is a proven negative integer.

StringsFirstCharactersCompare.summary:
`strncmp()`/`strncasecmp()` with a literal prefix and a hard-coded length that
does not match the literal's length compares too few (or too many)
characters — usually a leftover after editing the literal.

StrlenInEmptyStringCheckContext.summary:
Measuring a string's length only to know whether it is empty
(`strlen($s) > 0`, `!mb_strlen($s)`, `if (strlen($s))`) is indirect and
slower than comparing with the empty string. Suggest an identity comparison
with `''` instead, casting to string when the value is not known to be a
string.
StrlenInEmptyStringCheckContext.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|--------|------|---------|--------|
| (none) | | | Operand order follows the global comparison style (`regular` default / `yoda`). |

StrtokStateClobbered.summary: Detect starting a second two-argument strtok sequence between an initial sequence call and its one-argument continuation on the same reachable path.
StrtokStateClobbered.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

StrtotimeUsage.summary:
Two wasteful `strtotime()` idioms: parsing the literal `'now'` just to get the
current timestamp (`time()` does that directly), and passing `time()` as the
base timestamp, which is already the default.

SubStrShortHandUsage.summary:
`substr()` / `mb_substr()` accept a negative length ("stop N characters before
the end") and treat a missing length as "up to the end". Computing the length
as `strlen($s) - something` is therefore either replaceable by a negative
constant, or entirely unnecessary.

SubStrUsedAsStrPos.summary:
Checking a prefix by cutting it out with `substr($s, 0, …)` and comparing the
piece is the long way of asking "does `$s` start with this?". The idiomatic
form is a position search compared strictly against `0`
(`strpos($s, $prefix) === 0`), or its case-insensitive variant when the cut
piece was case-folded first.
SubStrUsedAsStrPos.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | | | Operand order of the fix follows the global comparison style (`regular` default / `yoda`). |

SuspiciousAssignments.summary:
Groups six independent checks for assignments that are most likely mistakes:
writes lost to a switch fall-through, compound operators that repeat their
target (`$n += $n + 1`), parameters overwritten before ever being read,
`=+`/`=-`/`=!` typos, values written twice in a row, and array destructuring
of something that is not an array.

SuspiciousBinaryOperation.summary:
Flags binary operations that are almost certainly not what the author meant:
`instanceof` against a trait, identical operands, `==` used as a statement,
`>=` typed instead of `=>` in an array, a comparison placed inside a call's
parentheses, negated comparisons on nullable values, `??` after a cast or
`!`, concatenation with an array literal, hard-coded booleans in `&&`/`||`,
and mixed `&&`/`||`/assignment precedence.
SuspiciousBinaryOperation.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `VERIFY_CONSTANTS_IN_CONDITIONS` | bool | `true` | Enables D9. |
| `VERIFY_UNCLEAR_OPERATIONS_PRIORITIES` | bool | `true` | Enables D10. |

SuspiciousFunctionCalls.summary:
A string comparison function called with the same expression as both
operands always yields "equal" — typically a copy-paste slip where one side
should have been a different variable.

SuspiciousLoop.summary:
Two loop mistakes: a `for` condition section with several comma-separated
expressions (only the last one decides whether the loop continues), and loop
variables that silently overwrite a parameter of the enclosing function or the
variable of an outer loop.
SuspiciousLoop.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `VERIFY_VARIABLES_OVERRIDE` | bool | `true` | Enables the parameter and outer-loop clash checks (D2–D4). |

SuspiciousReturn.summary:
A `return` inside a `finally` block discards whatever the `try` block was
doing on its way out: its own return value is replaced and any exception in
flight is swallowed. When the `try` block itself returns or throws, this is
almost always a bug.

SuspiciousSemicolon.summary:
A lone `;` used as the body of an `if`/`elseif`/`else` or of a loop makes that
body empty; the block that follows then runs unconditionally (or only once,
after the loop). This is nearly always an accidental semicolon.

SwitchContinuationInLoop.summary:
PHP treats `switch` as a loop structure for `continue`, so a bare `continue`
inside a `switch` only leaves the `switch` (like `break`) instead of starting
the next iteration of the surrounding loop. `continue 2` is what was meant.

SysvMessageExceedsReceiveCapacity.summary: Identify msg_receive whose positive maxsize is smaller than byte length of proven same-queue same-type successfully sent nonserialized constant string, without MSG_NOERROR. Serialized or competing messages exclude.

SysvMessageSerializationMismatch.summary: Identify msg_receive when local successful msg_send on same queue and exact positive matching type uses a different serialize flag. Require known flags, no unknown queue operation and no competing-sender evidence; unknown message selection excludes.

TempnamDirectoryFallbackUnchecked.summary: Detect tempnam result used for sensitive content under an explicitly enabled required-directory contract without verifying its parent directory.
TempnamDirectoryFallbackUnchecked.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

TernaryOperatorSimplify.summary:
A ternary whose branches are the literals `true` and `false` merely restates
its condition. When the condition is a binary expression, the ternary can be
replaced by the condition itself, its negation, or a boolean cast.

ThrowRawException.summary:
Throwing the base `\Exception` class gives callers nothing specific to catch;
a more specific (SPL) exception class communicates intent better. Separately,
throwing a standard-shaped exception without any constructor argument loses
the diagnostic message.
ThrowRawException.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| REPORT_MISSING_ARGUMENTS | bool | true | Enables D3 (exceptions created without any argument). |

TlsHandshakePendingAccepted.summary: Identify stream_socket_enable_crypto result tested only !== false and followed by fwrite in accepted branch, with same stream proven nonblocking through successful stream_set_blocking(false). Only true confirms established handshake.

TraitInstantiation.summary: Instantiate a class using the trait.
TraitInstantiation.options: None. Use ordinary rule configuration to enable or disable this inspection.

TraitsPropertiesConflicts.summary:
When a class and one of its traits (or its parent class and one of its
traits) declare the same property, PHP only accepts it if both declarations
are compatible, and even then the duplication is fragile. Point out these
overlaps; when the two declarations are incompatible (PHP refuses to compose
the class), it is a real conflict.

TransactionEarlyReturn.summary: Detect a reachable normal return from a scope owning a successfully begun PDO transaction where neither commit nor rollback occurs on the exit path.
TransactionEarlyReturn.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

TransactionExceptionWithoutRollback.summary: Detect a caught exceptional path after an owned PDO transaction begins when the catch continues or returns with the transaction active.
TransactionExceptionWithoutRollback.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

TransferEncodingWithContentLength.summary: Choose a single HTTP message framing mechanism.
TransferEncodingWithContentLength.options: None. Use ordinary rule configuration to enable or disable this inspection.

TrimMaskUsedAsSuffix.summary: Detect trim, ltrim or rtrim using a literal extension-like mask beginning with a dot and containing at least two alphabetic characters.
TrimMaskUsedAsSuffix.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

TruncationAssumedToRewind.options: None. Use ordinary rule configuration to enable or disable this inspection.

TypeUnsafeArraySearch.summary:
`in_array()` and `array_search()` compare loosely unless their third argument
is `true`, so `'1abc'`, `1`, `true` and `'1'` can all "match". Asking for the
third argument forces the author to decide whether loose matching is really
wanted.

TypeUnsafeComparison.summary:
Loose equality (`==`, `!=`, `<>`) silently juggles types (`'abc' == 0` was
true before PHP 8, `'1e1' == '10'` is true). This rule asks for strict
comparison, offers a one-click switch when comparing against a non-numeric
string literal, and flags objects compared to strings that have no
`__toString()`.

TypesCastingCanBeUsed.summary:
Conversion helpers (`intval()`, `floatval()`, `strval()`, `boolval()`,
`settype()`), a string made of a single interpolated expression (`"$x"`), and
explicit `->__toString()` calls all perform a plain type conversion. A cast
expresses the same thing directly and avoids a function call.
TypesCastingCanBeUsed.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| REPORT_INLINES | bool | true | Enables the single-interpolation string check (D8–D9). |
| REPORT_TO_STRING_METHOD_CALLS | bool | false | Enables the `__toString()` call check (D10–D11). |

The upstream fixture enables both.

UmaskSetterReturnMisread.summary: Identify umask called with a known nonzero mask whose return is strictly compared with that same supplied mask, and inequality causes unconditional throw or explicit failure.

UnNecessaryDoubleQuotes.summary:
A double-quoted string that contains no interpolation and no escape sequence
behaves exactly like a single-quoted one. Single quotes make it obvious that
nothing is evaluated inside.

UnSafeIsSetOverArray.summary:
`isset()` mixes two questions: "does the key/variable exist" and "is it not
null". This rule points out single-argument `isset()` calls where a more
explicit construct says what is meant: a plain `!== null` comparison for
variables and declared properties, `array_key_exists()` for array keys, and
flags concatenated index expressions that should be computed beforehand.
UnSafeIsSetOverArray.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| SUGGEST_TO_USE_ARRAY_KEY_EXISTS | bool | false | Enables D10. |
| SUGGEST_TO_USE_NULL_COMPARISON | bool | false | Enables D8 and its fix. |
| REPORT_CONCATENATION_IN_INDEXES | bool | true | Enables D9. When off, such accesses go straight to D10. |

All upstream fixtures run with all three options **on** and regular comparison
style.

UndeclaredDynamicProperty.summary: Detect assigning a missing instance property on a resolved PHP 8.2+ class with a complete known hierarchy.
UndeclaredDynamicProperty.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

UnescapedHtmlOutput.summary: Detect request-derived text emitted inside a proven HTML text-node context without context-appropriate escaping.
UnescapedHtmlOutput.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

UninitializedTypedPropertyRead.summary: Detect reading a resolved typed instance property when every incoming path proves it remains uninitialized.
UninitializedTypedPropertyRead.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

UnitEnumJsonEncoding.summary: Detect json_encode receiving a resolved unit enum value without a JsonSerializable implementation.
UnitEnumJsonEncoding.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

UnknownInspection.summary:
A `@noinspection` suppression naming an inspection that does not exist (typo,
renamed or removed rule) silently suppresses nothing. Point it out so it can be
corrected or deleted.

UnknownNamedArgument.summary: Detect a named argument absent from every resolved target parameter list where no target has a variadic parameter.
UnknownNamedArgument.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

UnlinkFailureReportedAsSuccess.summary: Identify discarded unlink call immediately followed by unconditional return true in the same function.

UnnecessaryAssertion.summary:
Some PHPUnit assertions verify something the language already guarantees:
asserting `null`/emptiness on the result of a `void` function, or the class
or type of a value returned by a function with a declared return type. Also,
`->expects($this->any())` on a mock asserts nothing and can be dropped.

UnnecessaryCasting.summary:
A type cast whose operand already has exactly the target type, or a string cast
used as an operand of concatenation (which converts to string anyway), is noise.
Dropping it simplifies the expression.

UnnecessaryFinalModifier.summary:
`final` on a method is redundant when the class itself is `final` (nothing can
extend it) or when the method is `private` (it cannot be overridden anyway,
constructors and other magic methods aside).

UnnecessaryIssetArguments.summary:
`isset($m['a']['b'])` already implies that `$m` and `$m['a']` are set, so
listing those containers as extra `isset()` arguments next to the deeper
access is redundant. Drop them.

UnnecessarySemicolon.summary:
Stray semicolons — empty statements and the terminator right before `?>` in a
short echo tag — add nothing and are usually typos. Remove them.

UnnecessaryUseAlias.summary:
An import alias identical to the last segment of the imported name
(`use App\Mail\Sender as Sender;`) changes nothing. Drop the `as` clause.

UnpackBufferTooShort.summary: Provide enough bytes for the unpack format.
UnpackBufferTooShort.options: None. Use normal rule configuration to enable or disable the inspection.

UnpackedNamedArgumentCollision.summary: Detect an explicit or unpacked argument binding a parameter already certainly bound by a literal unpacked array on the same call.
UnpackedNamedArgumentCollision.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

UnqualifiedReference.summary:
Inside a namespace, an unqualified call such as `strlen($s)` must be resolved
at run time (namespace first, then global). Writing `\strlen($s)` lets the
PHP 7+ compiler bind it at compile time and, for a set of special functions,
replace the call by a dedicated opcode. The same holds for global constants
and for function names passed as string callbacks.
UnqualifiedReference.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REPORT_ALL_FUNCTIONS` | bool | false | Report every unqualified global function call (and every callback name), not only those in the opcode list. |
| `REPORT_CONSTANTS` | bool | false | Also report unqualified references to global constants. |

The rule is disabled by default.

UnreachableCatchClause.summary: An earlier broad catch can intercept every exception a later catch would handle. Put specific exception handlers before broader handlers.

UnserializeExploits.summary:
`unserialize()` on attacker-controlled data can instantiate arbitrary
classes (PHP object injection). Report calls whose input can be traced to
request data or raw decoders, and — on PHP 7+ — calls that do not restrict
the allowed classes.

UnserializeFalseAmbiguity.summary: A false unserialize result can represent the valid serialized boolean false. Do not classify decoding failure solely from that value.

UnsetConstructsCanBeMerged.summary:
`unset()` accepts several arguments, so consecutive `unset(...)` statements can
be collapsed into one call.

UnsupportedEmptyListAssignments.summary:
Since PHP 7.0 destructuring into a pattern that has no target at all
(`list()`, `list(, )`, `[]`, `[, ]`) is a compile-time fatal error. In a
`foreach` value position this is easy to miss.

UnsupportedStringOffsetOperations.summary:
Writing through a string offset as if it were a nested array
(`$str[0][1] = …`) or appending to a string with `[]` (`$str[] = …`) is a
fatal error since PHP 7.1. When the written-to value is known to be a string,
such writes are bugs.

UntrustedFilesystemPath.summary: Detect request-derived path components reaching file read/write/delete or include sinks without established canonical containment or finite filename selection.
UntrustedFilesystemPath.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

UntrustedForwardedClientAddress.summary: Detect HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR-derived address used in an access-control comparison without established trusted-proxy validation.
UntrustedForwardedClientAddress.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

UntrustedHeaderValue.summary: Detect request-derived data reaching a response-header value without a dominating CR/LF rejection or safe construction summary.
UntrustedHeaderValue.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

UntrustedInclusion.summary:
Including a file by a relative path makes PHP search `include_path` (and the
current working directory), so a different file than intended can be loaded.
Anchor paths with `__DIR__` (or rely on autoloading).

UntrustedLdapFilter.summary: Request data inserted directly into an LDAP filter can alter its syntax. Escape values for the LDAP filter context.

UntrustedNetworkDestination.summary: Detect request-derived destination reaching curl, URL stream reads or equivalent network sinks without a proven outbound destination policy.
UntrustedNetworkDestination.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

UntrustedShellCommand.summary: Detect request-derived data reaching a shell-command sink in syntax-capable position without proven appropriate argument escaping or strict validation.
UntrustedShellCommand.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

UntrustedSqlConstruction.summary: Detect request-derived data reaching a resolved SQL execution sink as SQL syntax without parameter binding or proven context-appropriate validation.
UntrustedSqlConstruction.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

UntrustedXmlExternalEntityExpansion.summary: Expanding external entities in request-controlled XML can expose external resources. Disable that capability for untrusted documents.

UntrustedXmlWriterRawContent.summary: Write untrusted XML content as escaped text.
UntrustedXmlWriterRawContent.options: None. Use normal rule configuration to enable or disable the inspection.

UnusedConstructorDependencies.summary:
A private property that is assigned in the constructor but never touched by
any other method of the class (or its traits) is dead state — typically a
leftover injected dependency. Point at the constructor assignments.

UnusedGotoLabel.summary:
A `goto` label that no `goto` statement targets is dead code; it only
suggests control flow that does not exist. Remove it.

UnvalidatedRedirectTarget.summary: Detect request-derived data reaching a Location header without a proven permitted-local-target or finite destination policy.
UnvalidatedRedirectTarget.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

UploadClientMimeTrusted.summary: Detect acceptance of an upload based solely on $_FILES entry type compared to an allowed MIME string without server-side content inspection.
UploadClientMimeTrusted.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

UselessReturn.summary:
Two pointless `return` forms: a bare `return;` as the very last statement of a
function body (the function ends there anyway), and `return $local = expr;`
where the assignment to a local variable can never be observed after the
function has returned.

UselessUnset.summary:
Calling `unset()` on a function parameter only destroys the function's local
binding: the caller's value (whether passed by value or by reference) is
unaffected, and the local goes away at return anyway. Such an `unset()` is
almost always pointless.

UsingInclusionReturnValue.summary:
Using the value produced by `include`/`require` (a file that `return`s
something) couples code to file layout and hides dependencies. Prefer explicit
objects or functions; inclusion should be a standalone statement.

UsortDiscardsRequiredKeys.summary: Detect usort on a statically keyed array followed by access through an original nonsequential integer or string key that cannot exist after reindexing.
UsortDiscardsRequiredKeys.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

Utf8ByteTruncation.summary: Detect substr on a literal valid UTF-8 string with statically known offsets selecting an incomplete code-point byte sequence.
Utf8ByteTruncation.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

ValidatedBooleanFalseRejectedAsInvalid.summary: Identify FILTER_VALIDATE_BOOLEAN result compared strictly with false in a branch that unconditionally throws or returns explicit failure, when JSON-like known input is a valid false spelling; FILTER_NULL_ON_FAILURE and null comparisons exclude. Unknown input alone is insufficient to prove intent.

ValidatedIntegerZeroRejected.summary: Detect FILTER_VALIDATE_INT result tested for falsiness when zero is permitted by configured min/max bounds.
ValidatedIntegerZeroRejected.options: None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

VariableFunctionsUsage.summary:
`call_user_func()` / `forward_static_call()` with a callable that is known at
the call site can be written as a direct call (`$fn(...)`, `Cls::m(...)`,
`$obj->m(...)`), which is faster and analysable. Likewise
`call_user_func_array()` / `forward_static_call_array()` with a literal
argument array can pass the arguments inline.

VaryHeaderOverwritesEarlierDimensions.summary: Retain the earlier Vary dimensions. This opt-in inspection applies the policy stated in Detection.
VaryHeaderOverwritesEarlierDimensions.options: None. Enabling the rule declares the policy stated in Detection; the rule is disabled by default.

WeakMapValueRetainsKey.summary: Store a value that does not retain the WeakMap key. This opt-in inspection applies the policy stated in Detection.
WeakMapValueRetainsKey.options: None. Enabling the rule declares the policy stated in Detection; the rule is disabled by default.

WorldWritablePermission.summary: World-write permission lets other users modify a configured sensitive file. Remove that permission when the project's file policy forbids it. This inspection is disabled by default because the intended policy or use can vary.
WorldWritablePermission.options:
| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| sensitivePaths | list | `["**/*.pem", "**/.env", "**/config.php"]` | Configure the explicit policy evidence described in D1. |

WriteToReadOnlyStream.summary: Open the stream with write access.
WriteToReadOnlyStream.options: None. Use ordinary rule configuration to enable or disable this inspection.

XPathIgnoresDefaultNamespace.summary: Unprefixed XPath names do not select elements in a nonempty default namespace. Register and use a prefix for that namespace.

XPathQueryFailureDereferenced.summary: Check the XPath query result before accessing its nodes.
XPathQueryFailureDereferenced.options: None. Use normal rule configuration to enable or disable the inspection.

XmlParseZeroComparedWithFalse.summary: Identify strict comparison of xml_parse result to boolean false. The API returns integer zero on failure; loose false and strict zero comparisons exclude.

XmlParserNeverReceivesFinalChunk.summary: Identify xml_parser_free on a locally created parser after at least one xml_parse call, with no xml_parse true final argument and no xml_parse_into_struct completion. Unknown parser aliases or paths exclude.

XmlReaderAttributeCursorNotRestored.summary: Restore the XMLReader element cursor before element operations. This inspection is disabled by default; enabling it selects the stated policy.
XmlReaderAttributeCursorNotRestored.options: None. Use normal rule configuration to enable or disable the inspection.

XmlWriterAttributeAfterContent.summary: Identify writeAttribute or startAttribute on same resolved XMLWriter after text/writeElement in its current element, with no new startElement or endElement. Maintain bounded local element stack; unknown writer calls invalidate state.

XmlWriterMemoryOutputInUriMode.summary: Identify outputMemory on a locally created XMLWriter whose latest successful open operation is openUri. Failed open or unknown state exclude.

XslTransformationFailureConsumed.summary: Identify transformToXML result on a resolved XSLTProcessor passed directly or unchanged to file_put_contents or echo without rejecting false.

ZipCloseFailureUnchecked.summary: Writing an archive is not complete until finalization succeeds. Check the close result before returning success. This inspection is disabled by default because the intended policy or use can vary.

ZipEntryIndexPastEnd.summary: Use an existing ZIP entry index.

ZipEntryNameCollision.summary: Make ZIP entry replacement explicit. This opt-in rule applies the policy described in Detection.

ZipEntryStreamUsedAfterArchiveClose.summary: An entry stream depends on its containing ZIP archive remaining open. Consume the stream before closing the archive.

ZipExtractionExceedsConfiguredBudget.summary: Validate ZIP extraction against configured limits. This opt-in rule applies the policy described in Detection.
ZipExtractionExceedsConfiguredBudget.options:
- `maxExpandedBytes`: positive integer; default `20971520`.
- `maxEntries`: positive integer; default `1000`.

ZipFirstEntryTreatedAsMissing.summary: Distinguish a missing ZIP entry from index zero.

ZipOpenTruthyResult.summary: ZIP opening returns true for success and integer codes for errors. Check for true explicitly instead of using truthiness.

ZipSourceRemovedBeforeArchiveClose.summary: Keep ZIP source files until the archive closes.
